correctness.rationale: For the fixed language of positive words {epsilon}∪a{a,b}*, the given binary transitions A=(a:00,b:10) and B=(a:002,b:120) produce strongly connected automata with strict f-positive distance corner 0. Product z=(0,0), q=(0,2) have exactly length-three positive routes z->q via abb and q->z via aba, while positive words shorter than three are just a,aa,ab and cannot traverse either pair; hence equality 3=3 defeats strict f-corner inheritance. aba nevertheless resets all six product states, so this does not contradict product synchronizability. The universal five-state minimum follows by classifying all two-state positive-corner automata (four Type I reset-a automata, one Type II identity-a/reset-b), verifying every 2x2 type pair retains its corner and singleton factors cannot create failure. Independently enumerated 16 two-state binary automata, found exactly 5 with corner 0 and all 25 two-by-two pairs good, and checked the 2x3 witness metrics and reset. The fixed alphabet and positivity-function restriction is essential.
